posts.text:
A velvet worm hunts with a glue gun.

Two jets of slime fire from nozzles by its head, reach prey up to a foot away, and set in seconds.

The body doing this has barely changed in hundreds of millions of years.
comments: The slime hardens around whatever it hits and traps it where it stands. Velvet worms are one of the closest things alive to a true living fossil.

posts.text: Worst shed you've dealt with, fur or scales?
comments: Snake keepers, did the eye caps come off with it, or is that the part that went wrong?

posts.text:
The immortal jellyfish does not simply refuse to die. It demolishes itself first.

A stressed Turritopsis dohrnii settles, collapses its bell into a blob called a cyst, and rebuilds as a juvenile polyp within 24 to 72 hours.

That polyp then buds off new jellyfish.
comments: A full-grown adult is about 4.5 mm across, roughly a pinky nail, with a bright red stomach showing through a nearly transparent bell.

posts.text:
Hoatzin chicks hatch with two working claws on each wing.

Knocked out of the nest, a chick drops into the river, hauls itself out, and climbs back up the branches hand over hand.

The claws are gone by adulthood.
comments: Adults get called the stinkbird for a different reason. They ferment leaves in an oversized crop, the same trick a cow's stomach uses, and a meal can take up to 45 hours to pass.

posts.text: Does your pet tolerate baths, enjoy them, or treat them as betrayal?
comments: Follow-up: how long does the grudge last afterwards?

posts.text:
Most vipers strike, inject and let go, then track the prey down once the venom has worked.

The Gaboon viper often does not let go. It bites and keeps hold.

On a forest floor, that means a meal less likely to stagger off somewhere it cannot follow.
comments: That holding-on habit is also why a bite on a person is so much worse than the fang length alone would suggest.

posts.text:
The yeti crab grows its own food.

Bacteria live in the dense, hair-like bristles on its claws. The crab combs them off with its mouthparts and eats them.

It waves its claws through the water to keep the crop alive.
comments: The waving stirs fresh oxygen and chemicals past the bacteria so they keep growing. Yeti crabs turn up at deep sea methane seeps and hydrothermal vents, where there is nothing else to eat.

posts.text: Is your pet allowed on the furniture? Be honest.
comments: For the 'not allowed' crowd: where is your pet sitting right now?

posts.text:
A captive-bred poison dart frog is effectively harmless.

The frogs do not make their toxins. They collect them from wild mites and ants and store them in skin glands. Raise one on fruit flies and springtails and the poison never arrives.

So is it still a poison dart frog?
comments: That is why keeping one is possible at all, and why a wild-caught animal is a completely different proposition.

posts.text:
Pangolins have no teeth, so the stomach does the chewing.

Its far end is thick and muscular, lined with inward-pointing keratin spines, and usually holds small stones the pangolin swallowed.

Together they grind whole insects apart like a bird's gizzard.
comments: The scales are keratin too, the same protein as your fingernails. In seizures logged between 2016 and 2024, scales made up 99 percent of every confiscated pangolin part.

posts.text: Who does your pet think it belongs to? Honest answers.
comments: Bonus round: is it the person who feeds it, or the person who ignores it?

posts.text:
A frilled shark stays pregnant for up to 42 months.

Three and a half years. The longest known gestation of any vertebrate.
comments: The eel-like body and roughly 300 trident-shaped teeth in 25 rows have barely changed for tens of millions of years, which is where the living fossil label comes from.

posts.text:
Constriction does not crush bones, and it is not suffocation.

Measurements on constricting snakes show the pressure is enough to stop blood circulating, and circulatory arrest kills far faster than suffocation would.

The snake tightens as its prey breathes out.
comments: Each exhalation gives away a little more room, and the prey never gets it back. Anacondas also give birth to live young, often twenty to forty at a time, each already around half a meter long.

posts.text: What noise does your pet make that nobody believes until they hear it?
comments: Guinea pig people, describe it without using the word wheek.

posts.text:
Hoopoe chicks defend the nest by aiming their droppings at whatever gets too close.

The mother starts it. She coats the eggs in a secretion from a gland near the tail, and the smell has been compared to rotting meat.

It seems to work on predators.
comments: The secretion also appears to keep feather-damaging bacteria in check, so the stink is doing two jobs at once.

posts.text:
Amano shrimp larvae die unless they reach brackish or marine water in their first days.

Adult amano shrimp die from even a small, accidental dose of salt.

Same animal. So how does anyone breed them at home?
comments: The salt phase belongs to the larvae alone. Try to acclimate a mature amano into a saltwater tank and it dies.

posts.text: What's the oldest pet you've ever had, and how old did it get?
comments: Tortoise and parrot people, you may need to show your work.

posts.text:
The white crust on a marine iguana's head is sea salt it sneezed out.

It is the only lizard that forages in the ocean, grazing algae off submerged rocks, and the kidneys alone cannot clear that much salt.

A gland above each eye filters it from the blood. Then it sneezes.
comments: The crust dries white across the snout and the top of the head, which is why so many of them look dusted in chalk while they warm up on the lava.

posts.text:
Crop milk is not milk in any mammalian sense. No lactose, no mammary gland.

A Victoria crowned pigeon chick still lives on nothing else for its first days, and both parents make it, from cells lining the crop.
comments: Pairs usually raise a single chick, and both birds sit the egg, the male through the day and the female overnight. The bird itself runs about 75 cm long and up to 2.5 kg, a pigeon the size of a turkey.

posts.text: What's the weirdest thing your pet eats on purpose?
comments: Degu keepers get a free pass. Eating their own droppings is a nutritional requirement for them, not a confession.

posts.text:
A sarcastic fringehead settles a border dispute mouth to mouth.

The fish is rarely longer than 8 inches but can stretch its mouth to about four times its closed size. Two rivals press their gaping mouths together.

The one with the smaller mouth backs down first.
comments: It is a small, territorial fish, and the wrestling match is the whole contest. Nobody gets bitten, the smaller mouth just leaves.
